messages:
sara: Heads-up — saw p99 spike on /generate yesterday evening after the throughput bump. p50 looks fine but tail doubled.
ben: Which model/route and timeframe? any change in seq length distribution?
kevin: Observed between 19:10–20:05 UTC. Spike correlates with a set of long-context customer requests (seqs > 1200).
kevin: Profiled a few samples — kernel selector picked an optimized attention kernel for seq<=1024, but for >1024 it falls back to generic attention (no fused kernels) and matmul paths. That fallback explains the 2.5–3x latency delta.
ben: Oof. Do we have the profile snippet?
sara: Paste from perf trace:
```
# sample trace (simplified)
2026-03-15T19:22:41Z route=/generate req_id=abc123 seq_len=1600
kernel_select: attention_fused? false
exec_path: fallback_generic_attention -> matmul_gemm -> kv_cache_lookup (lock wait 12ms)
latencies: total=820ms p50=120ms p99=780ms
```
maya: Also noticed KV cache lookups are contending for locks when many concurrent microbatches target the same session. That amplifies tail.
ben: So there are two contributors: kernel fallback at large seq and kv-cache contention + lock waits.
kevin: Short-term mitigation ideas:
- cap max_tokens per request on this public route to 1024 for high-throughput tier
- enforce truncation policy (drop tokens from prompt end or summarize) before enqueueing
- limit microbatch size for long-seq requests (microbatch max 4) to avoid huge single-op matmuls
- increase kernel timeout and pre-warm optimized kernels for sequences near threshold
maya: For KV cache: try per-session shard to reduce lock hotness, and add async KV reads for cache-miss path to avoid blocking the main thread.
sara: Proposal for immediate action (canary rollout tonight):
1) per-route config: max_tokens=1024, truncation=truncate_prompt_tail, truncate_threshold=2048
2) microbatch_policy: max_microbatch_items=8, prefer_small_batches=true when seq_len>512
3) KV cache: reduce lock scope + increase eviction TTL for short sessions
4) telemetry: add tag "truncation_applied" and measure request success/quality delta
ben: Can we try an A/B with 50% traffic on dedicated canary pool vs current to measure p95/p99 and quality?
kevin: I can run the A/B. Need the exact config snippet to inject into rollout system.
sara: Config for canary (paste into rollout tool):
```
route: /generate
model_variant: llama-2-13b-opt
max_tokens_per_request: 1024
truncation_policy: prompt_tail_truncate
truncate_threshold_tokens: 2048
microbatch: {
  mode: conditional,
  max_items: 8,
  seq_based: true,
  seq_threshold: 512
}
kv_cache: {
  lock_mode: shard_per_session,
  async_lookup_on_miss: true
}
observability: {
  tag_truncation: true,
  sample_traces_on_tail: 100
}
```
maya: Add a guard: if truncation_applied && response_quality_delta > 2% degrade, rollback automatically.
ben: Also add a fallback-model policy: if latency > SLO at p95 for 1 minute, route to low-latency quantized variant and mark trace.
infra-bot: deploy-canary job started for /generate canary pool (job id: dpl-20260315-09). Logs will appear in #eng-runtime-deploys.
kevin: I'll run the perf job and return with p95/p99 delta after 2 hours. @sara remind me to add the kernel metric for fallback count.
sara: @kevin thanks — I'll own the telemetry dashboard and split by seq buckets.
maya: Follow-ups: RFC for permanent truncation policy + per-route sensible defaults; longer-term: extend kernel selection to include optimized path for 1024<seq<2048 by landing fused matmul attention or tiling.
ben: Sounds good. If this reduces tail without hurting quality too much, we can keep the per-route cap as default for high-throughput tier.
sara: Action items: @kevin run A/B and post results, @maya file RFC, @ben add fallback-model policy to rollout config, infra-bot will handle canary.
kevin: On it. Will update with numbers ~21:30 UTC.
sara: Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
